title: Battery & power
blurb: Not charging, draining fast, sleep and wake problems.

remedies.title: Laptop isn't charging
remedies.why: A faulty charger, cable or socket, a weak USB-C charger, or a battery-care setting that stops at 80%.

steps.text: Try another wall socket, and check the charger's light; try another cable/charger of the right wattage.
Charge from the laptop's own charger, not a dock or a phone charger; USB-C chargers under ~45 W may only slow the drain.
"Plugged in, not charging" at 80% is often battery care on purpose (maker's app, or Optimised Battery Charging on Mac).
Check Battery settings and the battery health.
Check the battery's state in Power & battery settings.
Shut down, unplug, hold power 15 seconds, then plug in and charge while off.

remedies.escalate: If the battery swells (case bulges, trackpad lifts), stop using it and tell IT.

remedies.title: Battery runs out too quickly
remedies.why: Bright screen, heavy apps and browser tabs, background sync, or a worn battery.

steps.text: See which apps use the most battery: Settings › System › Power & battery › Battery usage.
See battery usage and turn on Low Power Mode on battery.
Lower screen brightness and close apps you aren't using.
Check the battery's health; batteries wear out after a few hundred cycles.
Check what's busy in the background.

remedies.title: Battery empty after the laptop was closed overnight
remedies.why: The laptop wakes for updates and notifications in sleep, or something keeps it from sleeping.

steps.text: Shut down (or use Hibernate) for longer breaks or before putting it in a bag.
Power options › Choose what closing the lid does › Hibernate on battery.
Battery › Options: turn off "Wake for network access" and Power Nap on battery.
Unplug USB devices before closing the lid.

remedies.title: Computer won't sleep, or wakes up by itself
remedies.why: A device (mouse, network card) or app (video playing, a download) keeps it awake or wakes it.

steps.text: Set the sleep times: Settings › System › Power & battery › Screen, sleep & hibernate.
Stop the mouse waking it: Device Manager › Mice › Properties › Power Management › untick "Allow this device to wake the computer".
Set display sleep in Lock Screen settings, and "Prevent automatic sleeping" in Battery › Options.
Close video, music and big downloads; they keep the computer awake.

remedies.title: Computer won't wake from sleep (black screen)
symptoms: screen stays black after opening lid
remedies.why: A driver didn't resume properly, or the screen is asleep while the computer is awake.

steps.text: Press a key, move the mouse, then press the power button briefly once.
Press Windows+Ctrl+Shift+B to wake the graphics driver.
If nothing works, hold the power button 10 seconds; unsaved work is lost.
Update graphics and chipset drivers if it keeps happening.

remedies.title: Make the laptop faster on battery (or last longer)
remedies.why: Power mode trades speed for battery life.

steps.text: Settings › System › Power & battery › Power mode: Best performance when plugged in, Balanced or Best power efficiency on battery.
Battery › Low Power Mode: Only on Battery (or Never for full speed).
